subject: medicine
title: Tubulointerstitial, cystic and inherited kidney disease

steps.tx: Ask about recent penicillins, NSAIDs, proton pump inhibitors or **allopurinol** started weeks before fever with rash, arthralgia and **eosinophilia**. Record years of heavy analgesic use with haematuria and loin colic suggesting **papillary necrosis**. Note childhood urinary infections with scarring for reflux disease, and recurrent stones with haematuria for medullary sponge kidney. Trace family haematuria with stones and headache from subarachnoid bleeding for polycystic disease, and deafness with visual lens cone changes in boys for Alport syndrome. Map drug timelines against cystic family patterns.
steps.say: Ask about recent penicillins or anti inflammatory drugs, which are common triggers of allergic interstitial nephritis. Note fever with rash and joint pains starting weeks after a new drug, which suggests hypersensitivity within the kidney. Record years of heavy analgesic use with blood in urine and colic, which is typical of papillary necrosis. Note childhood urinary infections with scarring, which indicates reflux disease from early life. Trace family blood in urine with stones and head bleeds, which suggests polycystic kidney disease. Ask about deafness with visual changes in boys, which is typical of Alport syndrome.

steps.tx: Feel the flanks for enlarged ballotable kidneys suggesting **polycystic disease**, and track blood pressure for hypertension in cystic and reflux disease. Look for oedema in proteinuric phases, pale tophi in gout with analgesic clues, and loin tenderness with colic in stone formers. Test hearing for sensorineural loss with tuning forks and inspect eyes for lenticonus with retinal flecks in suspected Alport syndrome. Dip urine for leucocytes with blood and protein, examine sediment for eosinophils with white cell casts, and chart **growth failure** in affected children.
steps.say: Feel the flanks for enlarged kidneys, which are typical of advanced polycystic disease. Track blood pressure at every visit, which is raised early in cystic and reflux disease. Look for swelling in proteinuric phases, which indicates glomerular injury with protein loss. Test hearing with tuning forks, which confirms sensorineural loss in Alport syndrome. Inspect the eyes for lens cone changes with retinal flecks, which supports inherited disease in young patients. Dip the urine for white cells with blood and protein, which guides further testing of tubules.

steps.tx: The composite image pairs an audiogram showing high frequency **hearing loss** with a lenticonus eye, retinal flecks and a **haematuria strip**. Sensorineural deafness with anterior lenticonus and retinal flecks is characteristic of Alport syndrome, where abnormal collagen affects ears, eyes and glomeruli. Blood on the dipstick completes the renal clue in a deaf child with visual change. Link ear, eye and urine findings whenever inherited **basement membrane** disease is suspected.
steps.say: The image pairs an audiogram with eye and urine findings, which together indicates inherited kidney disease. High frequency hearing loss on the chart is typical of Alport syndrome in young patients. Lenticonus with retinal flecks adds the eye clue, which supports a collagen basement membrane disorder. Blood on the dipstick provides the renal clue, which connects deafness with glomerular bleeding. Combine ear, eye and urine signs whenever inherited disease is suspected in clinic.

steps.tx: Find sterile pyuria with white cell casts and **eosinophiluria** in allergic disease, and measure creatinine to stage kidney injury. Show bilateral cysts with liver cysts on ultrasound for dominant polycystic disease, small scarred kidneys for reflux, and paintbrush nephrocalcinosis on CT for **medullary sponge** kidney. Confirm stone burden with CT, test PKD1 with PKD2 and collagen genes for inherited disease, and detect concentration defects with polyuria. Separate allergic disease that recovers, analgesic papillae that slough, reflux scars that shrink kidneys, and cystic kidneys that enlarge with **genetic counselling** for families.
steps.say: Find sterile urine with white cell casts, which suggests interstitial inflammation rather than bacterial infection. Detect eosinophils in urine, which supports allergic disease that often recovers after withdrawal. Show bilateral cysts with liver cysts on ultrasound, which is typical of dominant polycystic disease. Show small scarred kidneys for reflux and paintbrush calcification on CT, which indicates medullary sponge kidney. Confirm gene changes for polycystic and Alport patterns, which allows family screening and counselling. Measure creatinine to stage kidney injury, which guides referral and long term follow up.

steps.tx: Stop the culprit drug at once and add steroids for allergic interstitial disease that fails to settle. Give fluids with citrate to prevent stones, prescribe **tolvaptan** to slow dominant polycystic disease, and block proteinuria with **ACE inhibition**. Offer antibiotic prophylaxis for reflux with recurrent infection, and clear stones by lithotripsy or ureteroscopy. Bridge end stage kidneys with dialysis toward transplant. Never miss berry aneurysm headache with subarachnoid bleeding, never use unreviewed drugs in **pregnancy**, and counsel abstinence from analgesics. Follow blood pressure with kidney size and family screening.
steps.say: Stop the culprit drug at once, which allows allergic inflammation to settle quickly. Add steroids when recovery is slow, which helps severe hypersensitivity settle. Give fluids with citrate for stones, which reduces recurrence in sponge kidney. Prescribe tolvaptan for selected polycystic disease, which is used to slow cyst growth and decline. Offer antibiotic prophylaxis for reflux with recurrent infection, which prevents further scarring in childhood. Bridge end stage kidneys with dialysis toward transplant, which remains the definitive option for failure.
